ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R3-CP-01: swap-by-output +1 wei reserve inflation via totalAmountInFilled > amountIn in _splitAmountsAndFeesByHeight
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test performs 100 swap-by-output operations and verifies reserve0+feeBalance0 <= actual USDC balance and reserve1+feeBalance1 <= actual WETH balance. All assertions pass — the +1 wei allowance at line 1680 is properly recalculated into fees at line 1691, preventing reserve inflation.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R3-CP-02: Dust double-counting in swap-by-output path — dust tracked in ptrPoolState.dust0/dust1 AND sent to swapper via amountOut = totalAmountOutFilled
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test performs 50 swap-by-output ops then withdraws all liquidity. Pool solvency holds: reserve+fees <= actual balance. Code analysis: at line 1704 amountOut = totalAmountOutFilled is a LOCAL var only, swapCache.amountOut is NOT updated with dust in swap-by-output path (line 1676 only runs for swapByInput). Dust stays in pool, given to next withdrawing LP. No double-spend.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R3-CP-03: Dual addInRange double-counting in _calculateLiquidityStartAndEndHeights — add0 modified by side0 then consumed by side1
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test adds liquidity with addInRange0=true, addInRange1=true after swaps, then immediately withdraws. Withdrawal amounts <= deposit amounts. The check at line 349 uses originalAdd0 (captured before side0 modification) while the subtraction at line 353 uses the already-modified add0 — but the precision truncation at lines 360-362 absorbs any excess, and the position value is bounded by actual token deposits.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R3-CP-04: Unchecked underflow in _collectPositionSide at line 508 — consumedLiquidity - (liquidity - sideValue) could wrap
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test with two LPs, swaps to consume liquidity, LP2 removes first, then LP1 removes. Both withdrawals succeed and w0 <= AMM balance. The consumedLiquidity is always >= (liquidity - sideValue) because consumedLiquidity tracks total consumed across ALL positions at that height, and (liquidity - sideValue) is only the consumed portion of THIS position.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R3-CP-05: consumedLiquidity inflation via addLiquidity when startHeight < currentHeight at line 723
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test pushes currentHeight high via 30 swaps, then LP2 adds liquidity (which triggers consumedLiquidity += currentHeight - startHeight). Additional swaps and solvency check pass. The consumedLiquidity inflation at line 723 is correct because the LP deposits tokens covering the already-consumed range — the upstream addLiquidity function requires token deposits proportional to the full position range including consumed portions.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R3-CP-06: DynamicPoolType no access control — globalState[msg.sender] isolation but poolId collision
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Code analysis: DynamicPoolType uses globalState[msg.sender] for ALL state reads/writes. Two different callers creating same-parameter pools get the same poolId but access completely separate state because msg.sender differs. View functions also key on msg.sender. No cross-caller state leakage possible.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R3-CP-07: Fee growth stale initialization in _crossHeight — feeGrowthOutside set with stale global value during height increase
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test: LP1 adds, 30 bidirectional swaps generate fee growth, LP2 adds at new height, 10 more swaps, LP2 withdraws. Solvency holds. The fee distribution at lines 1911-1927 happens BEFORE _crossHeight at line 1993 within the same _increaseHeight loop iteration, so feeGrowthGlobal is already updated when height crossing initializes feeGrowthOutside.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R3-CP-08: Tail removal in _removeLiquidityFromHeight moves currentHeight down, inflating sideValue for remaining LPs
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test: LP1 and LP2 add, swaps consume liquidity, LP2 removes (may trigger tail branch at line 663), LP1 removes. LP1 withdrawal <= AMM balance, solvency holds. The currentHeight reduction at line 668 is correct: when the last position at a height is removed, currentHeight moves to the next active height below, ensuring consistent accounting for remaining positions.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R3-CP-09: SingleProviderPoolType zero-output swap with extreme price near MIN_SQRT_RATIO
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Outside primary scope for this run (SingleProviderPoolType not tested with mock hooks). The concern requires a malicious hook returning MIN_SQRT_RATIO+1. However, the limitAmount check in AMMModule prevents users from accepting zero output unless they explicitly set limitAmount=0, which is self-inflicted. Not a protocol vulnerability.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R3-CP-10: Linked list gas DoS via stale endHeightInsertionHint pointing to zeroed node
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test: LP1 adds, LP2 adds, LP2 removes (clears height pointers), LP3 adds with potentially stale hint. Gas used < 1M. Code analysis: line 809-811 detects zeroed-out nodes and resets traversal to root. Worst case is O(K) traversal with K active heights — bounded by total gas limit and proportional to attacker's own deposit costs.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: INV-SW02: No Profitable Round-Trip on Fixed Pool
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test swaps USDC->WETH then WETH->USDC at various sizes (1, 100, 10K, 50K USDC). finalUsdc <= initialUsdc in all cases. Pool fee of 300 BPS ensures round-trip always costs the swapper. Fixed-price math with rounding-up for input and rounding-down for output ensures protocol always wins.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: INV-SW03: Rounding Favors Protocol on 1-wei swaps
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test performs 200 sequential 1-wei USDC input swaps. AMM USDC balance never decreases. Either the 1-wei swap produces 0 output (reverts with ZeroValueSwap) or the protocol keeps the dust.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Add/remove liquidity round-trip rounding loss > 2 wei
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test adds 10K USDC + 10K WETH then withdraws all. deposit >= withdrawal and loss <= 2 wei per token. Fixed pool height math rounds correctly.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Pool solvency violation after mixed swap operations
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test: 2 LPs, 50 bidirectional swaps mixing input/output-based. reserve+fees <= balance holds for both tokens throughout. Also tested: multi-LP withdrawal solvency, full drain and restore, bidirectional swap stress test.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: 100% fee pool swap produces unexpected behavior
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test creates pool with fee=10000 BPS (100%). Swap attempt either reverts (expected — no reserve input) or succeeds with 0 output. No loss of funds.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C3: _splitAmountsAndFeesByHeight fails on 1-wei input or large input
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test: 1-wei input reverts with ZeroValueSwap (expected). 50K USDC input succeeds. Solvency holds after both.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C4: swapByInput succeeds with zero liquidity pool
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test: swap on empty pool reverts as expected. No tokens lost.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C5: swapByOutput with output > reserve drains pool
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test: output=0 reverts. output=reserve+1 either reverts or caps at reserve amount. Solvency holds.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C9: Fee-only collection without liquidity change causes accounting error
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test: Alice adds liquidity, Bob swaps generating fees, Alice calls collectFees. Solvency holds after fee collection.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If an attacker performs thousands of swap-by-output ops where totalAmountInFilled = amountIn + 1, the +1 wei per swap inflates reserves by 1000 wei total. This phantom reserve would make the pool think it has more tokens than it actually holds.
hypothesis_results.detail: The +1 wei allowance triggers fee recalculation via _calculateOutputLPAndProtocolFee(totalAmountInFilled), which correctly recomputes amountIn including the extra wei. AMMModule then collects exactly swapCache.amountIn from the user (line 2191) and verifies balanceInBefore + amountIn == balanceInAfter (line 2208). No reserve inflation occurs.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If dust is tracked in ptrPoolState.dust1 AND the swapper receives the dust amount via amountOut=totalAmountOutFilled, the pool pays out the dust to the swapper but also accumulates it for LP withdrawal — a double-spend.
hypothesis_results.detail: Line 1704 sets a LOCAL amountOut variable, NOT swapCache.amountOut. In swap-by-output path, swapCache.amountOut stays at the originally requested amount (line 1019). The local amountOut is only used for fee splitting (line 1733). Dust stays in pool reserves, given to first withdrawing LP via _accumulateDustToWithdrawal.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If add0 is increased by depth0 for side0, and then the side1 check uses originalAdd0 (smaller), the subtraction at line 353 operates on modified add0 (larger), potentially creating a position covering more liquidity than deposited tokens support.
hypothesis_results.detail: The check at line 349 uses originalAdd0 to verify the LP has enough token0 BEFORE the depth0 addition. The modified add0 at line 353 already includes depth0. The precision truncation at lines 360-362 (add0 -= add0 % precision0) absorbs any fractional excess. Position size is bounded by actual token deposits.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If LP2 removes first reducing consumedLiquidity via line 516, then LP1's removal at line 508 computes consumedLiquidity - (liquidity - sideValue) which could underflow in the unchecked block, wrapping to a massive uint256.
hypothesis_results.detail: consumedLiquidity tracks TOTAL consumed across all positions at a height. When LP2 removes, line 516 subtracts only LP2's consumed portion. LP1's consumed portion remains in consumedLiquidity. The subtraction at line 508 computes LP1's specific consumed amount which is always within bounds because consumedLiquidity >= sum of all active positions' consumed portions.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If an attacker adds liquidity with startHeight=0 on a pool where currentHeight is high, consumedLiquidity inflates by currentHeight units without requiring proportional token deposits, creating phantom reserves.
hypothesis_results.detail: The consumedLiquidity increment at line 723 is matched by the LP depositing tokens covering the full position range (startHeight to endHeight). The upstream addLiquidity flow (FixedPoolType.addLiquidity -> FixedHelper.depositLiquidity) calculates startHeight based on currentHeight and precision, and requires token0 deposit proportional to the range. No phantom reserves possible.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If two different callers create pools with same params, they get the same poolId but separate state via globalState[msg.sender]. A price oracle reading from the wrong caller's state could return wrong values.
hypothesis_results.detail: ALL state access in DynamicPoolType keys on msg.sender via globalState[msg.sender]. View functions pass an address parameter that IS used as the key. External integrators must call via the AMM contract (which is msg.sender), ensuring correct state isolation. No cross-caller leakage.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If _crossHeight initializes feeGrowthOutside with a stale feeGrowthGlobal (before current swap's fees are distributed), a position created at the new height would capture fees from before its creation via wrapping subtraction.
hypothesis_results.detail: In _increaseHeight, fee distribution (lines 1911-1927) occurs BEFORE _crossHeight is called (lines 1993+) within the same loop iteration. feeGrowthGlobal is already updated when the new height's feeGrowthOutside is initialized, preventing stale initialization.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If removing the tail position moves currentHeight down (line 668), remaining positions see increased sideValue (endHeight - currentHeight grows), allowing them to claim more unconsumed liquidity than actually exists.
hypothesis_results.detail: When the tail position is removed and currentHeight moves to nextHeightBelow (line 668), this correctly reflects that there is no more active liquidity above that point. The sideValue increase for remaining positions is matched by the actual tokens that were deposited for those positions. Pool solvency invariant holds.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If a malicious hook returns MIN_SQRT_RATIO+1, the double mulDiv in SingleProviderHelper.calculateFixedInput produces amountOut=0, and the user loses amountIn+fees for zero output.
hypothesis_results.detail: Users set limitAmount as slippage protection. With limitAmount > 0, AMMModule rejects zero-output swaps. Only users who set limitAmount=0 are affected, which is self-inflicted. The pool's reserves increase by the input, maintaining solvency.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If an attacker seeds K heights then removes them, passing stale hints forces O(K) traversal for honest LP insertions, creating a gas griefing vector.
hypothesis_results.detail: Lines 809-811 detect zeroed-out nodes and reset traversal to root, preventing infinite loops. The gas cost scales O(K) with K active heights. Attacker's cost to create K heights (deposit liquidity for each) is proportional to or greater than the victim's gas cost, making the attack economically unviable.

theft_theses.thesis: Extract value via swap-by-output +1 wei reserve inflation over thousands of transactions
Extract dust accumulated from swap-by-output operations by being first LP to withdraw
theft_theses.asset: Accumulated dust (bounded by 1 output unit per swap)

theft_theses.thesis: Inflate position range via dual addInRange to withdraw more than deposited
Trigger unchecked underflow in _collectPositionSide to claim inflated withdrawal
Inflate consumedLiquidity via addLiquidity to create phantom reserves for arbitrage
